title: Periodic Table Arrangement
content:
# Periodic Table Arrangement

## Learning Objectives

By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
- Describe how the Periodic Table is organised
- Explain the relationship between electron structure and position
- Identify metals, non-metals, and metalloids on the Periodic Table
- Explain why elements in the same group have similar properties

## Introduction

The **Periodic Table** is one of the most important tools in chemistry. It organises all known elements in a logical way, based on their atomic structure. Understanding its organisation helps predict how elements will behave and react.

## Key Concepts

### Organisation of the Periodic Table

The modern Periodic Table is arranged in order of increasing **atomic number** (number of protons).

[DIAGRAM: Simplified Periodic Table showing groups and periods]

**Key features:**
- **Periods** - horizontal rows (numbered 1-7)
- **Groups** - vertical columns (numbered 1-7 and 0, or 1-18 in IUPAC notation)
- Elements are placed so that elements with similar properties are in the same group

### Periods

A **period** is a horizontal row in the Periodic Table.

| Period | Number of Shells | Elements |
|--------|-----------------|----------|
| 1 | 1 | H, He |
| 2 | 2 | Li to Ne |
| 3 | 3 | Na to Ar |
| 4 | 4 | K to Kr |

**Key point:** The period number equals the number of electron shells.
- Period 2 elements have 2 electron shells
- Period 3 elements have 3 electron shells

### Groups

A **group** is a vertical column in the Periodic Table.

| Group | Outer Electrons | Name | Examples |
|-------|-----------------|------|----------|
| 1 | 1 | Alkali metals | Li, Na, K |
| 2 | 2 | Alkaline earth metals | Mg, Ca |
| 7 (17) | 7 | Halogens | F, Cl, Br, I |
| 0 (18) | 8 (or 2) | Noble gases | He, Ne, Ar |

**Key point:** The group number equals the number of electrons in the outer shell.
- Group 1 elements have 1 electron in their outer shell
- Group 7 elements have 7 electrons in their outer shell

### Why Groups Have Similar Properties

Elements in the same group have the **same number of outer shell electrons**.

Chemical reactions involve the outer shell electrons, so elements with the same outer shell configuration react in similar ways.

**Example: Group 1 (Alkali metals)**
- All have 1 outer electron: Li (2,1), Na (2,8,1), K (2,8,8,1)
- All are reactive metals
- All react with water to form hydroxides and hydrogen
- All form +1 ions by losing one electron

### Electron Configuration and Position

| Element | Electron Configuration | Period | Group |
|---------|------------------------|--------|-------|
| Carbon | 2, 4 | 2 | 4 |
| Chlorine | 2, 8, 7 | 3 | 7 |
| Calcium | 2, 8, 8, 2 | 4 | 2 |
| Argon | 2, 8, 8 | 3 | 0 |

**To find position from electron configuration:**
- Count the number of shells = Period
- Count electrons in outer shell = Group

### Metals, Non-Metals, and Metalloids

The Periodic Table can be divided into:

**Metals** (left and centre):
- Good conductors of heat and electricity
- Shiny (lustrous)
- Malleable and ductile
- Form positive ions

**Non-metals** (right side):
- Poor conductors (insulators)
- Often gases or brittle solids
- Form negative ions or covalent bonds

**Metalloids** (along the stepped line):
- Have properties of both metals and non-metals
- Examples: silicon, germanium
- Important in electronics as semiconductors

[DIAGRAM: Periodic Table showing metal/non-metal boundary]

### Special Groups

| Region | Name | Properties |
|--------|------|------------|
| Group 1 | Alkali metals | Very reactive, soft, low density |
| Group 2 | Alkaline earth metals | Reactive, harder than Group 1 |
| Groups 3-12 | Transition metals | Multiple oxidation states, catalysts, coloured compounds |
| Group 7 | Halogens | Reactive non-metals, form salts |
| Group 0 | Noble gases | Unreactive, full outer shells |

## Worked Examples

**Example 1:** An element has the electron configuration 2, 8, 6. Determine its position in the Periodic Table and state whether it is a metal or non-metal.

**Solution:**
- 3 shells → Period 3
- 6 outer electrons → Group 6
- Position in Period 3, Group 6 → This is sulfur
- Located on the right side of the Periodic Table → Non-metal

**Example 2:** Predict why all halogens (Group 7) form similar compounds like NaCl, NaBr, and NaI.

**Solution:**
All halogens have 7 electrons in their outer shell. They all need to gain 1 electron to achieve a full outer shell. Therefore, they all form -1 ions and react similarly with metals like sodium to form ionic compounds with similar formulae.

## Common Mistakes

- **Mistake:** Confusing periods with groups
- **Correct:** Periods are horizontal rows; groups are vertical columns

- **Mistake:** Thinking Group 0 elements have 0 outer electrons
- **Correct:** Group 0 elements have full outer shells (8 electrons, or 2 for helium)

- **Mistake:** Forgetting hydrogen is a non-metal despite being on the left
- **Correct:** Hydrogen is a special case; it's a non-metal placed with Group 1 due to having 1 outer electron

## Practice Questions

1. State what is meant by a 'period' and a 'group' in the Periodic Table. (2 marks)

2. Explain why sodium and potassium have similar chemical properties. (3 marks)

3. An element X has the electron configuration 2, 8, 8, 1.
   a) Identify which group X is in. (1 mark)
   b) Identify which period X is in. (1 mark)
   c) State whether X is a metal or non-metal. (1 mark)

4. Explain, in terms of electron structure, why elements in Group 0 are unreactive. (3 marks)

5. The elements sodium, magnesium, and chlorine are all in Period 3. State and explain one difference between sodium and chlorine. (3 marks)

## Key Terms Glossary

| Term | Definition |
|------|------------|
| Periodic Table | A table of elements arranged by increasing atomic number with similar elements in columns |
| Period | A horizontal row in the Periodic Table |
| Group | A vertical column in the Periodic Table |
| Alkali metals | The highly reactive metals in Group 1 |
| Halogens | The reactive non-metals in Group 7 |
| Noble gases | The unreactive gases in Group 0 |
| Metalloid | An element with properties between metals and non-metals |

## Summary

- The Periodic Table is arranged by increasing atomic number
- Period number = number of electron shells
- Group number = number of outer shell electrons
- Elements in the same group have similar properties because they have the same number of outer electrons
- Metals are on the left; non-metals are on the right
- The stepped line separates metals from non-metals
